grid_access.label: Transmission & Substation Access
grid_access.means: Distance to transmission lines and substations, weighted by voltage. A 500 kV line counts far more than a 69 kV one. This is the single biggest constraint on whether a large load can connect at all.
grid_access.caveat: HIFLD's national substation layer is no longer public, so substations come from OpenStreetMap; 78% carry a voltage tag.

grid_headroom.label: Interconnection Headroom
grid_headroom.means: Generation capacity already planned nearby. Proxies whether new load can actually be energised this decade rather than waiting years in a queue.
grid_headroom.caveat: SUBSTITUTE. The real measure is the interconnection queue (LBNL "Queued Up"), which blocks scripted access. Planned additions understate queue contention.

power_cost.label: Industrial Power Cost
power_cost.source: EIA v2 API, retail sales (industrial sector)
power_cost.means: Industrial electricity price in cents/kWh. Power is the dominant operating cost of a data center, so this compounds over the life of the facility.
power_cost.caveat: Joined at STATE level. Utility service territory polygons are in the restricted HIFLD set, so intrastate spread is not captured.

cooling_efficiency.label: Cooling Climate
cooling_efficiency.means: Annual cooling degree days, interpolated between stations. Cooler climates allow more free cooling, which lowers both PUE and water consumption.
cooling_efficiency.caveat: SUBSTITUTE for ASHRAE design wet-bulb, which is paywalled. CDD ignores humidity, so a dry and a humid site with equal CDD score the same when they should not.

network_latency.label: IXP Proximity
network_latency.means: Proximity to interconnection facilities, weighted by how many networks are present. Matters enormously for edge and inference workloads, barely at all for training clusters.

water_availability.label: Water Availability
water_availability.means: Baseline water stress in the containing basin. Evaporative cooling needs water, and a water-stressed basin means permitting risk and local opposition regardless of what the utility will sell you.

buildability.label: Terrain & Land Cover
buildability.detail: CONUS DEM plus 30 m land cover, areal fractions
buildability.means: Terrain slope and land cover combined. Scored on development cost and permitting risk: already-serviced open land is best, high-intensity urban is worst (no room), cropland scores below pasture because prime-farmland conversion is heavily contested, and wetlands are excluded outright.
buildability.caveat: Slope is sampled at ~1.4 km, so it screens out mountains but says nothing about whether a specific parcel is flat.

policy_climate.label: Policy & Incentive Climate
policy_climate.source: LLM research pass, every claim source-linked
policy_climate.detail: all 49 CONUS states, 5.1 of 6 fields cited on average
policy_climate.means: Tax exemptions, abatements, permitting speed, active moratoria, who pays for interconnection upgrades, and cooling-water restrictions.
policy_climate.caveat: Assembled by an LLM with mandatory citations; any field without a real source URL is dropped rather than guessed. Verify before relying on it for a decision.

hazard.label: Natural Hazard Exposure
hazard.means: Earthquake, flood, wildfire, hurricane, landslide, ice storm, heat wave and tornado risk. Siting-relevant hazards (quake, flood, fire) are weighted above design-solvable ones (tornado, hail) -- tornado alley hosts plenty of campuses.

generation_proximity.label: Generation Proximity
generation_proximity.means: Installed generating capacity nearby. Overlaps grid access by design, but a plant next door is not the same thing as a high-voltage line.

market_maturity.label: Existing DC Cluster
market_maturity.means: Existing data center density. Scored as an optimum rather than more-is-better: some neighbours prove the fundamentals work, too many mean you are competing for the same substation.

gas_access.label: Natural Gas Access
gas_access.means: Distance to gas transmission. Increasingly decisive because on-site or bridge generation is how large loads get energised ahead of a grid upgrade.

clean_power_potential.label: Renewable Resource
clean_power_potential.detail: sampled on a coarse grid, interpolated
clean_power_potential.means: Annual solar irradiance. Proxies how cheaply on-site or nearby renewable generation can be added to meet a clean-energy commitment.
clean_power_potential.caveat: Solar only. Wind resource is too spatially spiky to survive this interpolation and uses a separate, heavier API.

network_infrastructure.label: Broadband Infrastructure
network_infrastructure.means: Household internet subscription rate, as a proxy for whether real network infrastructure reaches the area.
network_infrastructure.caveat: SUBSTITUTE. FCC's Broadband Data Collection returns 403/405 on every public endpoint. ACS measures adoption, not availability, so it understates areas with good infrastructure and low uptake.

logistics.label: Highway Access
logistics.detail: interstates and primary arterials, weighted by class
logistics.means: Distance to interstate and primary highway. Transformers, chillers and gensets move by oversize road freight, and construction traffic has to get there too.

default.label: Balanced (calibrated)
default.description: Fitted against real campuses and known-bad sites.

ai_training.label: AI / HPC Training Campus
ai_training.description: Power-dominant. Latency is nearly irrelevant; cooling and interconnection headroom dominate.

edge_latency.label: Edge / Latency-Sensitive
edge_latency.description: Proximity to population and exchanges dominates; raw power scale matters much less.

sustainable.label: Low-Impact / Sustainability-Weighted
sustainable.description: Penalizes water stress and rewards renewable resource and cool climate. For siting under corporate ESG constraints.

flags.label: Elevated poverty rate - environmental justice review indicated
Active local data center moratorium reported

protected_lands.reason: Federal protected land / designated critical habitat

land_cover_wetland.reason: Majority true wetland. Clean Water Act section 404 permitting through USACE makes a large pad impractical. Soft rather than hard: at 5 km2 a cell that is 60% wetland may still hold a buildable parcel. Open water is deliberately NOT included - riverfront is desirable for cooling, and including it scored an operating Columbia River campus at zero.
